title: Five things that moved private markets.
intro: Five source-backed developments from the most recently completed week, with the valuation context that matters for private-market investors.

scoreboard_deals.summary: Nscale announced a $3.36B convertible financing, including an initial $2.36B tranche and a $1B Nvidia commitment expected in November.
Snorkel AI raised a $350M Series E at a $3.5B valuation.

items.text: On September 26, Bloomberg reported that Nubank was in talks to buy Monzo for £8–10 billion, roughly twice the £4.5 billion valuation set in an October 2024 employee share sale; the talks may not lead to a deal. The reported top end would make it one of the largest fintech acquisitions and reset the valuation benchmark for profitable digital banks.

On September 25, Nscale announced a $3.36 billion convertible-note financing led by Third Point, including a $1 billion commitment from Nvidia, with the notes converting into shares at an IPO. The raise puts a large new financing marker beneath its $14.6 billion March 2026 valuation and tests public-market appetite for capital-intensive AI infrastructure.

On September 22, Snorkel AI raised a $350 million Series E at a $3.5 billion valuation, according to TechCrunch. The round shows investors are assigning strategic value to the data and simulation layer that supports training and evaluating AI systems.

On September 23, Ema announced a $77 million Series B for its enterprise AI-agent platform, bringing reported total funding to $140 million. The financing points to continuing investor demand for software that can automate multi-step work inside established corporate systems.

On September 24, Databricks acquired Row Zero to bring governed spreadsheets into its Genie AI-coworker platform; the terms were not disclosed. For a reported $190 billion private company, the acquisition is a useful signal that product gaps in enterprise AI are increasingly being filled through startup M&A.
